liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Iko Iko** (2 reviews): Reviewer describes feeling of unity and shared energy with the crowd during the opener; Reviewer considers it a great opener [11][12]
- **Black Peter** (2 reviews): Reviewer cued up the show for it; Jerry's phrasing is expressive and unpredictable, showing his underrated blues playing; Attendee calls it the show's highlight [9][10]
- **Walkin' Blues** (1 review): Reviewer felt they glimpsed nirvana for a moment or two during it [11]
- **Big River** (1 review): Jerry's first dabbling with fiddly MIDI effects shows up here [7]
- **Let It Grow** (1 review): Reviewer liked it; also found the cowboy songs decent [12]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Bertha, Playin' and Terrapin opening the second set were nice but, like the show, punchless [10]

## Setlist highlights

- **Space**: cut on the recording [15]

## The recordings

- **gd1988-09-30.beyerM88.russjcan.94477.flac16** (recommended): source not stated; 19 songs; 140 min; rated 1.5/5 by 2 [1]. Said about its sound: Quality matches the taper's description; recommends listening before downloading; Disc one track ten has an odd mix: weak vocals and Weir's guitar far forward [1][10]
- **gd88-09-30.set1aud-set2sbd.miller.21093.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 17 songs; 124 min; rated 2.5/5 by 6 [2]. Said about its sound: First-set audience sound is remote and thin [7]
- **gd1988-09-30.142152.UltraMatrix.cm.sbd.miller.flac1644**: soundboard; 17 songs; 132 min [3]
- **gd88-09-30.set2-sbd.sacks.7585.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 74 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [5]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's first show; a friend's glow stick leaked into their eye during drums/space, causing a rough spell [6]
- Bongos were allowed in, and a drum session took place on the top track of the lawn during intermission [6]
- Commenter says Shoreline was built on a former garbage dump, and they lived nearby then [8]
- Reviewer found Jerry off, struggling with lyrics and playing, with the band out of sync [12]
- The following two nights sound much better, according to the uploader [1]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1988-09-30.beyerM88.russjcan.94477.flac16**: taped by Russ Cansler; transferred by Russ Cansler; source: Beyerdynamic M-88's XY60 with Sony WMD6-C (Maxell MX 90 No nr) Offical taping section front of lawn 140 feet away ,dead center Mic stand at 7 feet [1]. Also: Let It Grow was cut and patched from another source; a mic pop on track four was fixed [1]
- **gd88-09-30.set1aud-set2sbd.miller.21093.sbeok.shnf**: source: Set 1 Aud - Set 2 Soundboard Cassette >DAT> CDR> EAC> seekable SHN [2]
- **gd1988-09-30.142152.UltraMatrix.cm.sbd.miller.flac1644**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: UltraMatrix SBD > Cassette Master (TDK MA-XG90) [3]. Also: Let It Grow patch from 8:41 to end comes from a Nakamichi CM700 front-of-board cassette master, via Bill Reutelhuber [3]
- **gd88-09-30.set2-sbd.sacks.7585.sbeok.shnf**: source: Set 2 Soundboard Cassette >DAT> CDR> EAC> seekable SHN [5]. Also: Second-set soundboard source circulates, taped by Sacks lineage (shnf file gd88-09-30.set2-sbd.sacks.7585) [6]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Shoreline Amphitheatre - September 30, 1988](https://www.dead.net/show/september-30-1988) [16]
